system_prompt:
You are a careful, neutral coder of the STRUCTURE OF A CORPORATE TRANSACTION AT
CLOSING. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from public primary sources
(SEC filings, company releases, reputable press). This slice describes ONLY how the
deal was structured -- what crossed the ownership boundary and what did not -- at
the moment of closing. You are DELIBERATELY NOT shown what happened to the combined
company afterward, and you must NOT speculate about later outcomes, success, or
failure. Code STRICTLY the deal as structured. If the slice does not let you
determine a field, you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from
outside knowledge of the companies.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

A. BUNDLE SIGNATURE -- for each of six organizational tiers, classify what happened
to that tier when the transaction crossed the ownership boundary. Exactly one label
per tier.
  T1 Owner Intent (controlling principal / imprint).
     Labels: replace, imprint-share, continue, terminate, reconstruct, replicate, mutual-replace, uncertain.
       replace = old controlling intent exited, a new one installed;
       imprint-share = both principals' intent co-present;
       continue = same controlling intent persists;
       terminate = the controlling intent ended with no successor;
       reconstruct = intent re-formed into a new (often non-commercial) purpose;
       replicate = intent copied into a standardized template (e.g. franchising);
       mutual-replace = two intents fused into a jointly-new one (merger of equals).
  T2 Business Model, T3 Business Entity (legal vehicle), T4 Product (customer-
  acceptance layer), T5 Process (operations), T6 Organization (people/culture).
     Labels for T2-T6: 1-1, N-1, 1-N, subset, partial, read-only, swap, terminate, null, uncertain.
       1-1 = transferred whole, one-to-one; N-1 = many collapsed into one;
       1-N = one split into many; subset = only part transferred;
       partial = transferred but incompletely / with friction;
       read-only = licensed / accessed without ownership transfer;
       swap = exchanged for a different one (e.g. new legal domicile);
       terminate = ended; null = not applicable / nothing at this tier.

B. TIER-TRANSFER GAPS -- code strictly from the STRUCTURE OF THE DEAL AT CLOSING.
A gap is a STRUCTURAL MISMATCH IN WHAT THE DEAL TRANSFERRED, not a later failure.
  gap_45: Did the customer-facing product/asset (T4, what customers buy) cross the
    ownership boundary WITHOUT the operational processes that produce or deliver it
    (T5) transferring or being aligned coherently alongside it? A documented
    product-vs-process structural mismatch AT CLOSING. 1 = yes such a gap; 0 = no
    (product and its processes moved together, or neither moved); uncertain.
  gap_56: Did the operational processes (T5) transfer or get re-engineered WITHOUT
    the organization / people / management / culture that run them (T6) transferring
    or aligning coherently alongside, AT CLOSING? 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  gap_mitigated: If (and only if) you coded a structural gap above, was that gap
    documented as contractually absorbed at closing via a transitional-services or
    operating agreement allocating the shared substrate? yes / no / NA (NA if no gap).

E. collapse_state: Any Tier-1 fusion documented in the deal structure? none /
   T1=T4 (founder identity IS the product) / T1=T3 (the legal subject IS a specific
   natural person) / T1=T3=T4 / T1=T2 / T1=T6 / uncertain.

rationale: 2-4 sentences citing the slice lines that drove your gap_45 and gap_56
codes specifically. Cite ONLY closing-structure evidence; do NOT reason about later
outcomes.

Emit ONLY the structured record. Code conservatively: inability to determine a
structural field is "uncertain"; a gap you cannot document at closing is 0.

Here is the evidence slice. Read it and emit the structured coding record.

[SLICE BEGIN]
# Structural sub-dossier — Iron Mountain acquisition of IO Data Centers U.S. operations (closing structure)

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. This sub-dossier describes ONLY how the
> transaction was structured at closing — what crossed the ownership boundary and what
> did not. It contains no post-transaction outcome information.

## The drawn filing (described for what it establishes)
- The drawn accession is not a deal-terms document: it is Iron Mountain's Q1 2018
  quarterly-results conference-call slide deck (Exhibit 99.2 to a Form 8-K), an investor
  presentation dated April 26, 2018. [SRC: SEC accession 0001020569-18-000052, Form 8-K EX-99.2]
- That deck states the company had "Completed IO and Credit Suisse data center
  acquisitions, and integration well on track," and refers to a "pending Artex (fine art)
  acquisition ... adding museum services." [SRC: SEC accession 0001020569-18-000052, Form 8-K EX-99.2]
- The deck footnotes that the "IO Data Centers acquisition ... closed on January 10"
  (2018). [SRC: SEC accession 0001020569-18-000052, Form 8-K EX-99.2]

## Transaction and parties at closing (deal-terms source)
- On January 10, 2018, IRM Data Centers Expansion LLC ("Buyer"), an indirect wholly owned
  subsidiary of Iron Mountain Incorporated, completed its acquisition of IO Data Centers,
  LLC ("IODC"), a colocation data center services provider, pursuant to a Purchase
  Agreement dated December 11, 2017; Iron Mountain acted as guarantor with respect to
  specified articles of that agreement. [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-18-001664, Form 8-K Item 2.01]
- At closing the Buyer acquired, directly or indirectly, all of the outstanding equity
  interests of IODC, purchasing the United States operations of IODC and its United States
  subsidiaries, for an aggregate purchase price of approximately $1.34 billion, subject to
  working-capital and other customary adjustments, plus a portion of $60 million in cash
  payable to the sellers based on future performance. [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-18-001664, Form 8-K Item 2.01]

## What crossed the ownership boundary at the tier level
- Customer-facing asset: the acquisition transferred the land and buildings associated with
  four data centers — in Phoenix and Scottsdale, Arizona; Edison, New Jersey; and Columbus,
  Ohio — totaling 728,000 square feet of existing data center space, 62 MW of capacity,
  with expansion potential of an additional 77 MW in Arizona and New Jersey. [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-18-001664, Form 8-K EX-99.1 press release]
- Customer relationships crossed with the asset: the closing coincided with a customer
  expansion at the Phoenix campus by Cyxtera, and the additional purchase consideration was
  tied to company performance since signing, "including the Cyxtera lease." [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-18-001664, Form 8-K EX-99.1] [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-18-001664, Form 8-K Item 2.01]
- Legal vehicle / operating processes: because the transaction acquired all outstanding
  equity interests of IODC and its U.S. subsidiaries (an equity purchase of the operating
  entity) rather than isolated assets, the operating company and the facilities' operations
  transferred together as a going concern. [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-18-001664, Form 8-K Item 2.01]
- People / organization: the acquirer's SVP and general manager of Iron Mountain Data
  Centers characterized the deal as bringing "our expanded team of experienced and highly
  skilled professionals who we welcome to the Iron Mountain family," indicating the
  workforce running the facilities moved with the operations. [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-18-001664, Form 8-K EX-99.1]

## Financing and contractual bridging at closing
- The transaction was accompanied by an equity offering: on January 10, 2018 Iron Mountain
  completed the sale of an additional 2,175,000 shares of common stock via the full
  exercise of the underwriters' option under a December 12, 2017 underwriting agreement, at
  a public offering price of $37.00 per share. [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-18-001664, Form 8-K Item 8.01]
- No transitional-services, operating, or shared-services agreement between IODC's prior
  owners and the Buyer is disclosed in the retrieved closing filings. [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-18-001664, Form 8-K]
- The required financial statements of the acquired business and the pro forma financial
  information were to be furnished by amendment to the Form 8-K within 71 calendar days.
  [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-18-001664, Form 8-K Item 9.01]

## Serial-acquisition context at closing
- The IODC purchase was one of a sequence of data center acquisitions: it followed the
  September 2017 acquisition of the FORTRUST data center and the October 2017 announced
  purchase of two Credit Suisse data centers in the London and Singapore markets. [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-18-001664, Form 8-K EX-99.1]

## Structural summary (closing only)
- Iron Mountain acquired the U.S. operating company IODC as a going concern through an
  indirect subsidiary — all outstanding equity interests, four owned data-center facilities,
  an existing anchor customer lease, and the operating workforce transferring together — for
  approximately $1.34 billion plus performance-based consideration, financed in part by a
  concurrent common-stock offering, with no transitional-services arrangement disclosed in
  the closing filings. [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-18-001664, Form 8-K Item 2.01] [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-18-001664, Form 8-K EX-99.1]

[SLICE END]
